summary:
ADR-0081 (Accepted 2026-08-31, narrowed 2026-09-07) makes qualification cadence an adaptive policy: a roughly daily review of per-gate cost, unique defect yield, detection delay and closure equivalence emits an immutable recommendation, never an automatic weakening. Low-yield expensive checks may move outward; valuable checks move back inward; hard boundaries (parent closure, freeze, release, cutover, rollback authority, security) cannot be optimized away; a defect missed by sparse qualification is charged to that cadence decision. Since 2026-09-07 routine delivery does not wait for the economics.

The performance-bounded flow design (Proposed) section 6 adds optimistic batching: select a batch only when its estimated value exceeds a robustness margin and its isolation plan fits the budget; on failure, classify, keep attributable passes, and split the ambiguous partition (binary splitting is the safe baseline); a parent failure with all-green partitions stays an interaction or flake finding. Speculation is limited to side-effect-free work and follows merge-queue invalidation. The first implementation batches checks for one candidate only.

Generic lessons: systems/batch-and-bisect, systems/queueing (OR14). ADR-0098 §11 tranche 2 (FS-GG/.github#5245) lists this record; the generic technique is a pack entry, the FS-GG instance stays here (§10).
title: Qualification cadence economics (ADR-0081) and optimistic batching with failure isolation
